text:
Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen's last two starts show both sides of his season. On Nov. 11 against Tampa Bay he was pulled after giving up five goals in 41 minutes, the worst night of his season. Eight days later in Washington he made the most of his first start since, saving about 1.6 more goals than the shots usually allow in a 6-3 win.

Over 13 starts he is 6-4-3 with an .872 save percentage, 1.8 goals worse than the chances he has faced deserve. The split tells the story: he's been very good on medium-danger shots, .906 against a league .862, and poor on the dangerous ones, .644 against .687. High-danger saves are where goalies separate, but they also take a full season to trust.

Last season he was 9.1 goals above expected in 35 games, and Evolving-Hockey had him at +19. That's the version Buffalo needs. Our range for his true save rate sits right around league average, so the next few starts should show whether Washington was a turnaround or one good night.
headline: Luukkonen steadies after a rough November night
